headline: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, an evaluation of AI agents on everyday-life tasks
summary: OpenAI introduced LifeVal, an evaluation of AI performance on everyday-life tasks selected using American and multinational time-use datasets and supplemented by a demographically representative survey that the public page says included 3,995 respondents, while the linked paper’s methods section specifies n=3,837 for the willingness-to-pay survey; the difference is unresolved. Its public page reports selected task scores of 90.4%–100% on illustrated workflows, but does not identify which model produced the examples or provide an overall aggregate result or detailed open protocol. The design and scores are first-party; independent replication and real-world user outcomes are not established.
